target_customer: Founders, operators and small teams who want a hosted personal AI agent (current product); the Winter 2020 customer is not documented in opened sources
problem: Setting up and hosting an open source OpenClaw agent and connecting it to many apps is hard, so users want a managed AI assistant that handles email, calendars and research (current positioning).
business_model: Monthly subscription tiers for a managed OpenClaw agent platform (Basic 20, Pro 50, Max 175 USD per month per the company site, with a conflicting 10 USD Basic on its llms.txt)
product_category: Managed AI agent hosting and personal AI assistant

founders.name: Kevin Joo
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page. No background found in opened sources.

founders.name: David Shi
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; bio reads building protocols for distributed intelligence.

technical_complexity.rationale: Current product is hosting and integrating an existing open source agent framework with many app connectors; the 2020 product is not documented, so the rating reflects the present offering only.

defensibility.rationale: OpenClaw is MIT licensed so any host can run the same codebase, and many managed hosting rivals exist with price comparisons published.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not assessable for 2020; the present market has many OpenClaw hosting and agent products such as KiloClaw.

market_need_then: Not documented for the Winter 2020 period; sources only describe the 2026 managed OpenClaw market and one aggregator listing an agent platform product dated 2020-10-24.

branding.brand_signature: Your AI chief of staff tagline

brand_strength.rationale: The name Operator is generic and shared by other companies including YC W20 Operator Labs listings and HiOperator; no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.from: Winter 2020 product, not documented in opened sources (one aggregator describes an agent creation platform)
pivots.to: Managed OpenClaw AI agent hosting and assistant
pivots.why: Not stated; the current YC tagline and site describe OpenClaw agents, a project that did not exist in 2020

outcome_analysis: Operator.io is listed as active with six people and no public funding found. Its current product, a managed OpenClaw agent assistant sold by subscription, differs entirely from anything that could have existed in Winter 2020, so the company evidently changed direction, but the dates and reasons are not public. With no funding data and low defensibility in a crowded hosting market, the outcome cannot be rated.
notes: Founded year unknown. No funding round found; Crunchbase returned 403 and aggregators show only a placeholder seed stage, and Altss amounts are paywalled. YC lists a separate Operator Labs page with the same founders, so the entities overlap. The company site is operated by Operator Research, Inc. Round Funded is a reconstruction and was not used. No dated competitor sources for the batch period were found. Pricing conflicts between operator.io pages (Basic 10 versus 20 USD).
